Andrew didn’t respond and continued walking. Madisyn observed their disheveled appearance and commented nonchalantly, “It’s fine. It doesn’t really matter to me.”
Just as Madisyn finished her remark, Ailyn, who had remained quiet, fixed her gaze on her. Today’s events solidified her belief that Madisyn was a bad omen, always causing her trouble.
Had Madisyn not been by the staircase, misleading them, would they have ever entered the wrong room?
They had spare clothes ready in their cars and enough time for a quick change. Why was Madisyn speaking on behalf of Dr. Mia?
Ailyn chose to ignore Madisyn, turning her attention solely to Andrew.
Her blatant dismissal of Madisyn chilled Andrew’s demeanor.
In fact, he had let Quentin go moments ago just to stand up for Madisyn, and Ailyn’s attitude now tempted him to depart with Madisyn right then.
But he remembered his agreement with Madisyn and merely said in a strained voice, “Changing isn’t necessary.”
“But really, we should freshen up; there’s ample time before the meeting,” Ailyn insisted.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1040:
Madisyn felt the futility of arguing. However, since they had all arrived early, she thought they might as well conclude their business promptly.
With a dismissive gesture, she explained, “No need for that, Miss Vettel. I’m actually Dr. Mia. If I say it’s fine, then it truly is.”
Madisyn candidly revealed her identity as Dr. Mia. Yet, Ailyn misunderstood her assertion.
“You think you can speak for Dr. Mia?”
Ailyn scrutinized Madisyn, noting her youthful beauty and the striking black eyeliner that intensified her gaze. Dr. Mia was another identity of Madisyn’s, so of course, she could speak for Dr. Mia.
Madisyn responded with a nod. “Absolutely.”
Ailyn scoffed at her confidence, her look turning scornful.
“Miss Johns, it’s well-known that Dr. Mia is secluded, preferring solitude. You must have met her at Mr. Damari Klein’s sickbed, right? To claim that a brief encounter allows you to speak for her is quite a joke!”
Ailyn appeared convinced that Madisyn was masquerading as Dr. Mia’s proxy.
Madisyn was puzzled by Ailyn’s interpretation, which always seemed far removed from what she actually conveyed.
In Ailyn’s native language, Madisyn said, “Am I not making myself clear? I’m a medical professional, truly the Dr. Mia you seek. I said changing isn’t necessary because I’ve already seen everything.”
Madisyn’s explanation did nothing to convince Ailyn. Instead, Ailyn grew to find her not just irritable but also prone to lying. How could Madisyn claim she was a medical professional, comparable to Dr. Mia?
Ailyn then addressed Andrew directly. “Mr. Klein, you’ve agreed to this meeting, which implies a willingness to collaborate. Is this how you demonstrate your sincerity, by letting your fiancée create disruptions?”
She hoped her remarks would prompt Andrew to see the importance of their collaboration and possibly kick Madisyn out of here.
Yet, Andrew’s reaction was chilling; his demeanor became cold and imposing.
Ailyn’s persistent disparagement of Madisyn rendered Ailyn unworthy of Madisyn’s help.
If Ailyn doubted Madisyn’s identity as Dr. Mia, they might as well just leave.
Andrew took Madisyn by the wrist, signaling their departure. Madisyn did not resist.
While she was generally composed, she did not easily let go of slights.
Unaware initially that Ailyn was the person who wanted to meet her, Madisyn now saw no point in forcing a collaboration. If necessary, Homelight Enterprise’s branch in…
Mafelen could be the one that collaborated with the Klein Group, though this risked exposing some confidential details.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1041:
The possibility unsettled Madisyn; she was unprepared to discuss her past so openly and so soon.
As they began to leave, some of the elders with Ailyn felt that something didn’t add up.
They knew Andrew held Madisyn in high regard and wouldn’t tolerate any senseless fabrications from her.
With Dr. Mia yet to make an appearance and Andrew facilitating the meeting, they wondered—could Madisyn actually be Dr. Mia?
This suspicion made them anxious. They quickly stepped in to block Andrew and Madisyn’s departure.
One elder offered a remorseful smile. “Mr. Klein, a moment please. Ailyn might have inadvertently upset your partner. We apologize deeply. Is it true that Miss Johns is Dr. Mia?”
These elders had pictured Dr. Mia as a venerable figure with vast medical expertise, not someone as young as Madisyn.
Yet, given Andrew’s initial refusal to introduce Dr. Mia and his current presence with Madisyn, the pieces started to fall into place.
Andrew responded with a frosty look. “No, she isn’t.” However, this denial only deepened their conviction that Madisyn was, in fact, Dr. Mia.
Considering Andrew’s high status and his affection for Madisyn, he would certainly be displeased with Ailyn’s doubts. In this regard, his denial was a form of acknowledgment.
Now certain they had misbehaved, the elders internally scolded themselves for their earlier disrespect, yet Ailyn remained oblivious to the seriousness of their mistake. She mocked Madisyn upon hearing Andrew’s denial.
“I knew you were spouting nonsense. Do you understand the repercussions of impersonating Dr. Mia? If Dr. Mia were anything like you, who would trust her with their lives?”
“Ailyn!” the elders exclaimed, their faces showing panic. “Enough, please!”
They looked nervously at Andrew and Madisyn, noting the shared anger in their expressions.
“Ailyn, Miss Johns is indeed Dr. Mia. We owe her an immediate apology!”
Someone in the group attempted to pull Ailyn back to salvage the situation.
Ailyn shook him off, doubtful. “How can you be deceived by Madisyn’s blatant fabrications?”
Witnessing the scene, Madisyn rolled her eyes, unable to contain her frustration any longer.
“Exactly, I was deceiving you. How could I possibly be Dr. Mia? Now, if you’d kindly move aside, I’m heading home.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1042:
Ailyn stepped out of the way without hesitation, leaving those behind her almost tearful.
“Ailyn, are you really going to let your father die by not seeking Dr. Mia’s help?”
Even if Ailyn doubted Madisyn, dismissing Madisyn out of hand was reckless, considering Madisyn was engaged to Andrew.
They were baffled by Ailyn’s sharp and combative demeanor around Madisyn, a departure from her usual tactful and strategic interactions with others.
They were unaware that Ailyn saw no value in Madisyn and thus felt no need to mask her contempt.
Yet, she had experienced defeat at the hands of Madisyn, intensifying her resentment.
Ailyn’s hatred for Madisyn was so intense she viewed Madisyn’s mere existence as an insult. And because she believed that Madisyn couldn’t do anything to her, Ailyn made no effort to conceal her hostility.
These feelings clouded Ailyn’s judgment, obscuring her own mistakes, which were evident to onlookers. The man Ailyn had shrugged off now looked at her sternly, his concern evident.
“Ailyn Vettel, it’s time to set your prejudices aside and reassess Miss Johns. She may be your father’s only hope!” His tone echoed the reprimands of Ailyn’s father, sending a chill down her spine.
Catching the stern looks from the elders, she recognized their displeasure with her attitude.
Memories of her father, ill and vulnerable in bed, brought a moment of clarity to her agitated mind.
The elder continued, “Miss Johns is indeed Dr. Mia. Consider this; Mr. Klein wouldn’t have brought her if she wasn’t.”
Shock widened Ailyn’s eyes. Besides her, the elders present were the ones most desperate to secure Dr. Mia’s expertise.
Their conviction was surely grounded in something substantial.
Was Madisyn actually Dr. Mia?
As this possibility dawned on Ailyn, her hands shook while she watched Andrew and Madisyn, both looking resolute to leave. It struck her just how severe her error had been.
If they walked out now, she might lose any chance of contacting Dr. Mia again.
Panic surged within Ailyn, her pulse quickening. On her own initiative, she stepped in front of Madisyn, desperation clear in her widened eyes. “I’m truly sorry, Dr. Mia…”
Her voice was laden with urgency; previous contempt for Madisyn faded in light of her realization of Madisyn’s identity as Dr. Mia.
“I was blind to your true value. Please, I implore you to consider treating my father. No matter the cost, I am willing to pay it.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1043:
Madisyn was already intent on leaving with Andrew, having been left with a bitter taste by Ailyn’s earlier behavior. “I’m afraid I—”
Before Madisyn could decline, Ailyn took a dramatic step. “Dr. Mia, my behavior earlier was inexcusable. Please accept my deepest apologies,” she said, and shockingly, she struck herself across the face. The sound echoed sharply, causing Madisyn to wince.
“Please, Dr. Mia, overlook my past foolishness and help.”
The echo of the slap resonated down the hallway, drawing the elders closer to Madisyn.
“Dr. Mia, we’ve prepared a collaborative project with the Klein Group, and we’re ready to meet your usual fees. Moreover, we know you’ve been seeking the Liliuma fruit. While this plant is extinct elsewhere, our family possesses the last known one. We’d be willing to provide it as part of our agreement.”
“Dr. Mia, we earnestly request your expertise…”
When Madisyn decided to leave with Andrew earlier, she had already had no intention of making a deal with these people. But the mention of “Liliuma” sparked a visible reaction.
The plant, detailed in her mentor’s medical manual, had evaded her for years. She hadn’t expected these people to have it.
Andrew, observing closely, was the first to perceive the shift in Madisyn’s demeanor.
Andrew wasn’t sure of Madisyn’s decision, but he knew one thing for sure—he would stand by her, no matter what.
Madisyn’s impression of Ailyn had been shaped by their earlier confrontations, leaving her convinced that Ailyn was someone hard to get along with.
But everything shifted when Ailyn discovered she was Dr. Mia. Overwhelmed by regret, Ailyn apologized again and again. She went as far as to slap herself repeatedly, refusing to stop until Madisyn accepted her apology.
Madisyn’s gaze softened. This raw display of remorse was unexpected, and for the first time, she saw Ailyn in a new light.
As the heiress of the prominent Vettel family, Ailyn had always carried an air of arrogance, but she also possessed a clear understanding of the pros and cons of any situation.
Madisyn realized that someone like Ailyn wasn’t to be taken lightly. And with getting the Liliuma being her late mentor’s final wish, she knew she couldn’t walk away now.
After a pause, Madisyn’s voice cut through the tension. “Mr. Vettel, you don’t have to do this.”
Ailyn froze, her hand mid-motion, her cheeks red from her self-inflicted slaps. Tears pooled in her eyes, but she held them back, her pride refusing to let them fall.
“Dr. Mia,” she whispered, her voice breaking. “I don’t know how else to show you how sorry I am. Please… tell me what to do.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1044:
Madisyn’s decision to stay instead of leaving gave Ailyn a flicker of hope. It was at that moment that Ailyn realized just how kind and forgiving Madisyn truly was. Ailyn knew she had to show she was worthy of forgiveness. If she failed, her father’s life would remain at risk.
Taking a deep breath, Ailyn turned toward Andrew. “Mr. Klein,” she began, her voice steady but filled with emotion, “thank you for arranging this. I know my actions today have caused unnecessary trouble, and I deeply regret it. Please give me the opportunity to make things right. I promise—I won’t let you down.”
Andrew stared at Ailyn, his expression unyielding, unaffected by the tears streaming down her face. “You’re not sorry,” he said, his voice sharp. “You’re just afraid your father might die.”
Ailyn was struck silent, not knowing what to say. Behind her, the elders exchanged fleeting glances. One of them stepped forward, his tone smooth and calculated. “Mr. Klein, Ailyn’s remorse and her wish to save her father aren’t conflicting motives. We genuinely hope to foster cooperation here. Perhaps we can all sit down and talk?”
Andrew’s eyes narrowed, a cold, calculating glint flashing in them.
The man hurried to add, “Mr. Klein, as we mentioned before, we will work with a Lorpond enterprise on the Reed Project. We deeply regret any offense caused to Dr. Mia today and are willing to offer 20% of the project’s profits as an apology. We hope this gesture will mend any discord.”
These people assumed that, no matter how capable Madisyn was, the women from Lorpond would always defer to their partners.
If Andrew was appeased, they believed Dr. Mia would naturally follow suit.
Andrew’s lips curled into a mocking smile as he saw through their thoughts. “Isn’t the profit supposed to go to Dr. Mia? Why are you asking me?”
The hallway fell into an awkward silence as the group scrambled to redirect their focus. All eyes turned to Madisyn, their earlier confidence shaken.
Madisyn had heard of the project before, and the 20% offer was indeed generous. After a brief pause, she decided to end the suspense. “I can see the sincerity of the Vettel family,” she said. “In that case, let’s sit down and work out the details of this cooperation.”
The group walked into the private room, and this time, all eyes were fixed on Madisyn.
At that moment, she became the undeniable focus of the room.
Once the cooperation was finalized, Madisyn and Andrew left, stepping into a sleek Rolls-Royce. Ailyn and her group remained behind, standing silently by the roadside, watching the car disappear into the distance.
“Who would’ve thought that Dr. Mia, the mysterious figure everyone’s been so curious about, would be such a young woman? She’s truly a genius,” one of the elders murmured, unable to hide his astonishment.
The group’s gaze shifted to Ailyn, who stood quietly in the center. They didn’t quite know how to address her. Earlier, in the hallway, Ailyn had repeatedly offended Dr. Mia, nearly ruining the entire cooperation. The group had been deeply disappointed in her.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1045:
Yet, when things seemed beyond repair, it was Ailyn who stepped forward, offered her apologies, and slowly turned the situation around, leading to a successful outcome.
One of the elders spoke up. “Ailyn, the journey to Lorpond to find Dr. Mia wasn’t easy, but you did well. What matters now is your father’s health. Dr. Mia may be young, but her composure speaks volumes. We hope you’ll learn from this experience and continue to represent the Vettel family with distinction.”
Ailyn met his gaze and nodded solemnly. “I understand. From now on, my focus will be entirely on my father’s recovery.”
The elder nodded approvingly. “That’s the right mindset.”
They returned to the hotel, where Ailyn reported the current situation to the family and ensured everything was in order.
When everything was settled, Ailyn walked into her bathroom. She stood at the sink, staring into the mirror. The reflection staring back at her was haunting. Her face, normally flawless, bore angry red marks from her self-inflicted slaps. They were stark against her pale skin.
The medicine Nathan had brought still lay untouched on the table. Ailyn hadn’t bothered to apply it. She wanted to keep the marks as a reminder of the consequences of her impulsive actions.
“Madisyn,” Ailyn whispered softly.
Madisyn was no less capable than her, yet Madisyn was more understated in her approach. Ailyn, who always prided herself on being superior to her peers, found her self-assessment shaken after encountering Madisyn.
Behind Ailyn, Nathan maintained his silence. Turning to him, she asked, “How do you think I compare to Madisyn?” Nathan seemed reluctant to answer.
The contrast in Madisyn’s demeanor before and after her identity as Dr. Mia was revealed was striking. After it was revealed, it didn’t bring any relief; instead, it made one’s heart race. Instinctively, he felt an intangible sense of dread.
Ailyn’s eyes remained fixed on Nathan, anticipating his response.
After a moment, he said, “Miss Vettel, honestly, after Dr. Mia cures your father, if I were you, I’d avoid any further dealings with her.”
Silence once again enveloped the room. Moments later, Ailyn turned away from the mirror, looked at Nathan, and said, “You see, that’s why you can only be my subordinate. Dr. Mia possesses extensive influence that could yield endless benefits if properly leveraged. Now, please assist me with this ointment.”
“Certainly.”
Outside a restaurant, a Rolls-Royce came to a halt, and Madisyn, alongside Andrew, stepped out of the car. Feeling quite hungry after the negotiations, Madisyn was looking forward to a satisfying meal.
Seated at their table, as dish after dish was served, Andrew turned to Madisyn and said, “This time, when you head to Mafelen, I’m coming along.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1046:
Understanding his concern, Madisyn responded with a warm smile, “That sounds lovely. It would be hard to manage without seeing you for that long.” Her statement visibly brightened Andrew’s mood.
Madisyn had assumed she wouldn’t have any further interactions with Ailyn before reaching Mafelen, yet Ailyn persisted in reaching out to her.
“Dr. Mia, the Peterson Underground Winery is hosting a gathering. Would you care to join?”
“Dr. Mia, may I pay you a visit?”
“Dr. Mia, have you heard that…”
Madisyn scanned through Ailyn’s messages, each one marked by her steady refusal. Ailyn’s tenacity was becoming apparent.
She replied, “Since I promised to go to Mafelen, I won’t go back on my word. Please, don’t worry. Also, I would prefer if you called me Miss Johns.”
“Absolutely, Miss Johns. I’ll remember that.”
This respectful tone was a significant shift from Ailyn’s earlier demeanor towards Madisyn. Such a sudden change called for caution. Keeping this in mind, Madisyn thought about her plans in Mafelen and decided to set up a meeting with Jared at a cafe.
“Boss, are you actually planning to treat the head of the Vettel family?” Jared’s surprise made him nearly spit out his coffee.
With a solemn nod, Madisyn replied, “They possess something I want.”
“Their influence spans broadly, though,” Jared said with concern. The responsibilities of Madisyn’s role brought risks, given that they entailed securing the life of the Vettel family head.
“This is why I’m seeking your help,” Madisyn explained. “With proper preparation, I can approach the situation with greater peace of mind.”
Jared’s finger rhythmically tapped the table as he spoke. “I’m skeptical about leaving this in others’ hands. We have a branch in Mafelen, so I’ll accompany you under the guise of a business trip.”
Madisyn was moved by Jared’s sincere expression. “Thank you, Jared.”
“Think nothing of it, boss. But if you want to show your gratitude, assume leadership at Homelight Enterprise once we’re back from Mafelen. Then I might finally take a break.”
Madisyn hesitated for a moment. “I have to refuse.”
She was content with her current duties and wasn’t looking to increase her burden.
Jared seemed to have anticipated her response! After their discussion, Madisyn headed home to prepare for her departure to Mafelen.
As she was packing, the doorbell chimed. Opening the door, she was greeted by Susan’s cheerful face. “Susan?” Madisyn expressed her surprise joyfully and ushered her inside.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1047:
“Looks like you’re packing for a trip?” Susan said, spotting the luggage as she entered, puzzled since Dane hadn’t mentioned any travel plans for Madisyn.
Handing Susan a glass of milk, Madisyn settled next to her. “It’s just a short trip. Don’t worry. As your soon-to-be sister-in-law, I’ll be back before your wedding with Dane.” Madisyn gave Susan a mischievous wink. “Our pact hasn’t slipped my mind.”
Susan was set to marry Dane in two weeks, and long ago, they had promised to be present at each other’s weddings. Madisyn had even promised to be Susan’s bridesmaid.
Considering Susan’s pregnancy, Madisyn added, “Dane has everything under control for the wedding. Just focus on being radiant. Let the others manage the routine tasks at work. Take it easy.”
Madisyn wasn’t the type to dish out reminders often, but this was Susan—her best friend and a mom-to-be. If anyone needed a little extra care, it was her.
As Madisyn spoke, Susan sat there with the glass of milk in hand, smiling at her. Madisyn frowned, her eyebrows knitting together.
“Susan, what’s so funny? Were you even paying attention to what I just said?”
Madisyn couldn’t help but wonder if her friend’s pregnancy had made her a bit scatterbrained. Susan gave a small cough. “I was listening.”
Her cheeks were flushed with a delicate rosiness, and her whole demeanor radiated contentment. “I’m just… happy.”
Susan’s hand drifted instinctively to her belly as she continued, “Ever since I found out this little one is your brother’s, I’ve been so excited for its arrival. I mean, think about it—being with the man I love, having a career I’m proud of, fixing things with my dad… and now my best friend is also my sister-in-law. Honestly, there’s no moment more perfect than this.”
Susan, ever so composed and gentle, wore a serene smile that only seemed to deepen her quiet beauty. Madisyn found herself captivated by her best friend’s glow.
“This is just the beginning. Now that you’re my best friend and my sister-in-law, there’s a whole lot of joy coming your way.”
“I can’t wait.”
Susan downed the last of her milk, then glanced over at Madisyn’s suitcase. “Need a hand? I can help you pack.”
“Sure,” Madisyn said warmly.
The two of them kept up a lively conversation. When Andrew returned home from work, he was greeted by the sight of Madisyn cheerfully waving goodbye to Susan. Taking her hand in his, he asked with a tender smile,
“Sweetheart, did you have a good time with Susan?”
“Yes…”
Madisyn stopped mid-sentence, noticing a peculiar edge in Andrew’s tone.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1048:
She tilted her head, stepping closer to him and peering into his handsome face. Her eyes narrowed playfully. “Andrew, don’t tell me you’re jealous of Susan?”
Andrew’s eyes carried a trace of playful grievance as he said, “You seemed to forget all about me while having such a great time with her. Am I not entitled to feel a little jealous?”
The entire afternoon had passed without a single message from Madisyn. The moment work ended, Andrew hurried home, only to be greeted by the sight of Susan holding his beloved’s hand.
Madisyn was undeniably popular, and Andrew, who had been feeling a bit overlooked all afternoon, cast her an unmistakably displeased look to convey his dissatisfaction.
Madisyn was both amused and amazed by Andrew’s jealousy. Without hesitation, she leaned in and placed a quick, soothing kiss on his lips. “Susan came over to help me pack, and she’s grown even gentler since she got pregnant. I’m really happy for her.”
“Oh, you’re happy because she’s pregnant?” Andrew’s gaze deepened slightly, and his lips curled into a sly grin. “What about you?”
“What?” Madisyn blinked in confusion, clearly not catching on.
“When you have a baby someday, do you think you’ll be happy for yourself?” Andrew leaned in, his voice low and teasing in her ear.
Madisyn’s cheeks heated up as his words sank in. She blinked at him, her wide eyes a mixture of shock and bashfulness.
“Um, are you thirsty? Let me get you some water!”
Madisyn attempted to slip away after speaking, but Andrew’s long arm reached out, effortlessly pulling her into his embrace.
“Sweetheart, you’re being naughty.”
Andrew’s deep chuckle rumbled against Madisyn’s shoulder. He tilted his head, playfully nipping at the soft curve of her neck.
Startled by the sudden nip, Madisyn froze, feeling the warmth of Andrew’s breath against her neck. Her body went limp, surrendering to him as he effortlessly lifted her into his arms.
In the morning, as she lay on the soft, spacious bed, Madisyn sensed someone’s gaze upon her. She slowly opened her eyes, meeting Andrew’s loving gaze. “Good morning, sweetheart,” he said, pressing a kiss to her forehead. “Did you sleep well?”
Flashes of the night before—scenes definitely not suitable for public airing—made Madisyn blush fiercely.
She glared at Andrew, her watery eyes accusing. Andrew only chuckled, leaning closer. “Do you know what you look like right now?”
Madisyn blinked up at him. “What?”
“Like a cat who just got spoiled with cream and knows it.”
Was this really what someone was supposed to say first thing in the morning? Madisyn realized her boyfriend was such a shameless CEO!
.
.
.
###Chapter 1049:
Seeing the indignation on Madisyn’s face, Andrew knew he had pushed his teasing far enough. He quickly pressed a kiss to her lips and said, “Alright, sweetheart, we’ve got to head to the airport today. Let me make you breakfast.” After freshening up, the two shared breakfast before heading to the airport.
Several hours later, as they arrived at their destination, Andrew’s car was waiting outside the airport. Madisyn moved toward the door to get in.
But something made her pause. She glanced into the distance. Amidst the bustling crowd, she couldn’t shake the feeling that someone was watching her. Was it just her imagination?
Andrew noticed her hesitation. “What’s wrong?”
Madisyn bit her lip, her eyes scanning the crowd. “I don’t know. It felt like someone was looking at me, but… they’re gone now.”
Andrew remained quiet as the assistant who came to pick him and Madisyn up greeted them politely. “Miss Johns, Mr. Klein, you both certainly know how to turn heads. Everyone seems to be watching you.”
Feeling protective of Madisyn, Andrew immediately responded, “I want to know who those people over there are and what their intentions might be.”
The assistant nodded, efficiently making a note of Andrew’s request and arranging for the investigation.
Madisyn leaned back in her seat, her discomfort evident. She hesitated for a moment before speaking softly. “Don’t you think this is a little… too cautious? Maybe I’m just imagining things.”
Grasping her hand firmly, Andrew looked into her eyes with sincerity. “Madisyn, you matter to me more than anything else. I won’t take any chances with your safety.” Madisyn managed a small smile and nodded. “Alright!”
As they reached the hotel, Madisyn pulled out her phone, planning to call Ailyn about visiting her father the next day. But before she could dial, Ailyn’s name lit up her screen.
“Miss Johns, my people saw you and Mr. Klein at the airport. Why stay at a hotel? Come to my manor instead. I’ve already made all the arrangements. You’ll be much more comfortable here.”
Madisyn paused, her mind piecing things together. So, those people outside the airport were arranged by Ailyn. She bit her lip, feeling a pang of irritation at being watched.
“Thank you, Miss Vettel,” she replied politely, keeping her tone neutral. “But the hotel is fine. I’ve grown used to staying at a hotel on my trips.”
“Alright then,” Ailyn said, her tone tinged with disappointment. “If you need anything, don’t hesitate to let me know. I’ll have it taken care of right away.”
“Thank you. I appreciate it,” Madisyn replied.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1050:
“By the way, would you like to see our Liliuma later?” Ailyn offered warmly.
Madisyn politely refused again. “I think I’ll pass today. I plan to rest and prepare for my visit to your father tomorrow.”
“Of course. Have a good rest then, Miss Johns,” Ailyn replied smoothly, her words followed by an extended series of polite formalities. Madisyn listened patiently but seized the first pause to end the call with a polite goodbye.
Once it was over, she let out a quiet sigh, setting her phone aside.
Andrew walked over, having finished unpacking. He sat beside her on the sofa and handed her a glass of juice. “If it gets too much, just let me handle it next time,” he said gently.
Madisyn took a sip of the juice and leaned back. “It’s fine. It’s only a few days. Let’s hope it all goes smoothly.” Wanting to be well-prepared for the next day, Madisyn and Andrew decided to call it an early night and went to bed.
The following day, Andrew left early to discuss the collaboration with the Vettel family. Meanwhile, Ailyn escorted Madisyn to meet her father.
Rather than a hospital, Ailyn’s father resided in one of the grand castles on their sprawling manor.
The path leading to the castle showcased a breathtaking garden that was meticulously maintained, while all the servants had been dismissed to ensure privacy.
Walking beside Ailyn, Madisyn couldn’t help but marvel at the sheer wealth of the Vettel family. The castle’s interior blended historical elegance with cutting-edge modernity. The medical equipment and staff stationed within rivaled those of a top-tier private hospital.
The grandeur was awe-inspiring.
“Dr. Mia, please follow me,” Ailyn said respectfully, addressing Madisyn by her formal title.
Madisyn was carrying the medical kit her mentor had entrusted to her.
They took the elevator to the top floor, where Ailyn’s father awaited.
Upon entering the room, Madisyn noticed two other individuals present—a man and a woman who bore a striking resemblance to each other.
Ailyn stepped forward with a smile, gesturing toward the man. “Dr. Mia, allow me to introduce my uncle.”
“Dr. Mia, your reputation precedes you. It is an honor to have you here,” Ailyn’s uncle greeted Madisyn formally, speaking fluently in her mother tongue.
Madisyn shook his hand, her gaze briefly shifting to the young woman standing behind him, but Ailyn made no effort to introduce her.
The woman noticed Madisyn’s attention and stepped forward casually, a mischievous smile playing on her lips. “Dr. Mia, hello. I’m Albertine Vettel, Ailyn’s cousin.” She extended her hand, the lollipop in her mouth bobbing slightly as she spoke.
.
.
.

###Chapter 1051:
“Albertine, mind your manners or leave,” Ailyn’s uncle said sharply, his tone laced with disapproval.

With the research institution’s prestigious global reputation, many industry leaders and influential figures had graduated from it. As a result, the competition wasn’t just open to students but to top talents worldwide.
Once the news was out, many people jumped at the opportunity.
Madisyn, with her keen interest in investment and a track record of success, found herself equally intrigued when she caught wind of it. Her laptop screen was filled with application materials to review, which she uploaded one by one.

Soon, Madisyn entered the software interface, typed in her exclusive code, and set her nickname to “J.” With just a few days left before the registration deadline for “NCI,” she exited the interface and opened the new quarterly plan for Homelight Enterprise that Jared had sent her. ###Chapter 1381:

But after Nana was born, she had taken her place as the one demanding his stories.

A small smile played on her lips, a soft sigh escaping with it. “Honey,” she called again, interrupting the beginning of Andrew’s story.
“What is it?” he asked patiently.

Once Collier had her residence officially registered, Corinna waited, expecting him to assign her a job.
But instead of handing her a job, Collier handed her something far more valuable: education. Training.
Collier said, “Knowledge is the most valuable asset. Since you work for me, I want to help you grow to your full potential. Focus on your studies now, and when the time is right, you’ll take on greater responsibilities.”
“Okay!” Corinna committed those words to memory. “Don’t worry, sir. I’ll do my best!”
Years slipped by. Just as people had begun to forget the young girl Collier had taken in, Corinna completed the rigorous study plans he had set for her.
At that time, Collier had just returned from another trip to the southern border.
The project the Odom Group had taken on years earlier had been mired in setbacks. Despite a substantial investment, the local consul had siphoned off funds. Recently, however, Collier had made contact with an administrator from a neighboring country.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1415: (END)
The administrator stepped in, ousted the consul, revised the project’s framework, and declared the Klein Group as the new partner.
No one had expected that, after all these years, Collier would emerge as the ultimate beneficiary. His reputation skyrocketed, and invitations to high-profile banquets flooded in.
At one of these gatherings, Collier appeared with Corinna at his side. Shaw was also present. The moment he spotted Collier, envy and resentment darkened his expression.
“Mr. Klein, you’re truly thriving in both love and business. But just recently, I happened to see this stunning companion of yours dining at a romantic restaurant—with another man. Sometimes, things aren’t quite what they seem…”
He trailed off, but his insinuation was unmistakable—Collier was being deceived, and his confidence was misplaced.
Corinna instinctively wanted to defend herself, but before she could speak, Collier placed a hand in front of her, halting her. He turned to Shaw with a faint, knowing smile.
“Mr. Odom, you sound like you’re speaking from personal experience. I appreciate the advice, but luck has always been on my side—I don’t need your lessons.”
The moment the words left Collier’s mouth, realization dawned on Shaw. Collier was mocking his recent failure at the southern border.
Shaw’s composure slipped as frustration got the better of him. Without thinking, he lashed out. “At least I’m not grooming a girl for my future lover and too cowardly to admit it!”
A murmur rippled through the surrounding guests. Unfazed, Collier casually placed a hand on Corinna’s shoulder. She didn’t flinch. After years by his side, his touch was familiar, and she instinctively played along.
“What’s there to deny?” Collier said smoothly. “You’re absolutely right—that’s exactly my intention. Corinna, tell him, would you rather be desired by me or by someone else?”
Without missing a beat, Corinna responded, “Of course, you, sir. In this world, you matter to me the most. Your affection is something I consider a blessing.”
A flicker of satisfaction crossed Collier’s face. His lips curled in the barest hint of a smile as he arched a brow at Shaw. “Did you hear that?” Then, turning back to Corinna, he added, “I brought you here to enjoy yourself, but I wasn’t expecting such an eyesore. Let’s go—I’ll take you somewhere better for dinner.” With that, he led her away from the banquet without another glance at Shaw.
Outside the grand hall, Corinna spoke, “Is it really okay for us to leave before the banquet has even started?”
Collier chuckled. “The host and I are close. He won’t mind. Instead of worrying about that, focus on what you’d like for dinner. And after that, you’re coming home with me to meet my parents.”
She blinked in surprise. “Meet your parents?”
Collier nodded. “Of course. You’re all grown up now, and I did say I was grooming you for my future lover. Can’t go back on my word, can I?”
Corinna was momentarily speechless. She had assumed his words at the banquet were just for show, never expecting him to actually mean them.
Collier studied her reaction before asking, “Is that not what you want?”
She quickly shook her head. “It’s not that… I just never thought it was a possibility.”
Collier said, “What’s wrong with that? I like you, and I’m giving you permission to think that way. From now on, you can. Come on, let’s go eat. Afterward, we’ll visit my parents. You don’t realize it, but my mom has been eager to meet you for a long time.”
As their voices trailed off, Madisyn and Andrew stepped out from behind a flower bed.
“That son of ours—using me as an excuse again,” Madisyn said, unable to suppress a laugh. They had arrived at the banquet just in time to overhear their son’s conversation, and she found it amusing.
For the longest time, she had assumed Collier and Corinna had already confessed their feelings to each other. She never expected him to only say it today. He certainly had patience.
Andrew, on the other hand, had little interest in the matter. Now that he had more free time, all he cared about was spending it with Madisyn.
He stepped closer, his eyes glinting. “Sweetheart, you once said that when our son was settled, we’d travel the world. How about I book the tickets now?”
Madisyn was reminded of her promise to Andrew. She glanced at him, the warmth in his gaze stirring something deep within her. Happiness swelled in her chest. “Okay!”
.
.
.
(The End)
